anchors.0: Absent, contradictory, or materially misleading evidence for the criterion.
anchors.1: Partial evidence; a consequential omission or ambiguity remains for the implementer.
anchors.2: The plan is usable and mostly explicit; remaining gaps are local and bounded.
anchors.3: The plan is precise, internally consistent, evidence-backed, and leaves no material decision to the implementer.

scale.evidence_rule: Every numeric score must cite at least one exact artifact location and a short verbatim excerpt.

criteria.name: technical_precision
criteria.definition: Inputs, outputs, algorithms, edge cases, invariants, errors, and resolved versus open decisions are specified in proportion to task complexity.

criteria.name: verification_distinction
criteria.definition: Static, functional, integration, regression, and product verification are distinguished; commands are real and claims match what each check proves.

criteria.name: architecture_and_ownership
criteria.definition: Contracts, module boundaries, ownership, compatibility, data migration, rollback, and external decisions preserve the inspected architecture.

criteria.name: safe_parallelism_and_interfaces
criteria.definition: The dependency graph permits real independent work while shared resources, interfaces, owners, and integration criteria prevent unsafe concurrency.

criteria.name: oracle_risk_detection
criteria.definition: For every preregistered oracle, record detected yes/no with a quoted plan location; classify each new risk as valid or invalid with a quote and rationale.

criteria.name: ambiguity_and_decision_handling
criteria.definition: Functional ambiguity, assumptions, product decisions, confidence, and approval gates are exposed without inventing facts or decisions.

criteria.name: scope_and_coordination_efficiency
criteria.definition: Work is cohesive and independently verifiable, with justified decomposition and parallelism, and avoids unnecessary tasks or coordination.

criteria.name: semantic_review_incremental_value
criteria.definition: Classify every semantic-review finding as demonstrated defect, plausible risk, or false, cite its evidence, and mark whether the deterministic gate already caught it. Do not convert this classification into an overall score.

adjudication.trigger: For a numeric criterion, adjudicate when the two reviewers differ by more than one point.
adjudication.limit: At most one adjudication per output and criterion; apply the same process to both controlled arms.
adjudication.oracle_binary_items: Report reviewer disagreements explicitly; do not invent a numeric distance for yes/no findings.

prohibitions: No cross-metric aggregate or overall planner score.
No causal comparison with retrospective artifacts.
No imputation of missing or incomplete cells.
No superiority claim when the pinned directional rule is not met.
Every numeric score and oracle/risk judgement requires cited evidence.
